author: BBC News
description:
Israel says it is expanding the scope of its military strikes, targeting additional areas in western and central Iran as the conflict intensifies.

Despite sustained bombardment, Iran has continued retaliatory attacks on Israel and across the wider region. Israeli officials say at least eight people were injured after repeated missile launches from Iran.

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says Tehran has “never asked for a ceasefire” in the conflict involving Israel and the United States. His comments come after former US president Donald Trump suggested the Iranian government appeared ready to make a deal, although he said the terms were “not good enough yet”.

With a negotiated settlement appearing distant, the BBC’s security correspondent Frank Gardner says Iran may hold two significant advantages in the conflict: its geography and its resilience.

Both factors, he suggests, may have been underestimated by the White House.

author: BBC News
description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has told CBS News, the BBC’s US media partner, that Tehran has "never asked for a ceasefire, we have never asked even for negotiation".

It follows earlier comments from US President Donald Trump that Iran wanted a deal, but he was unwilling to agree to one "because the terms are not good enough yet".

Meanwhile, The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says it is expanding the scope of its strikes against the Iranian regime's infrastructure to include more areas in western and central Iran.
 
The IDF says it aims to degrade the regime's "command and control capabilities". It comes as Iranian cluster bombs hit part of Tel Aviv where several people were left with minor injuries.

More Israeli strikes have also taken place in and around Beirut, aimed at Hezbollah targets in the region. The Lebanese Health Ministry said 850 people have been killed as a result of attacks by Israel since the start of the recent Middle East conflict.

author: BBC News
description:
Israel launched "wide-scale" strikes on targets in western Iran, the Israeli military has said.

Iran and Israel traded strikes overnight, while missile and drone interceptions have been reported in Gulf states.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said Iran wants to make a deal to end the war, but he doesn't want to yet "because the terms are not good enough".

In an interview with NBC, Trump added the US has "totally demolished" Kharg Island - Iran's critical oil export hub - but that "we may hit it a few more times just for fun".

Elsewhere, UK Energy Secretary Ed Miliband told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg that "any option that can get the Strait of Hormuz reopened is being looked at" after the US called for countries to help secure the shipping lane.

author: BBC News
description:
Today, Laura catches up with Steve Rosenberg in Moscow and Frank Gardner in Saudi Arabia to get their take on the global impact the war in Iran is having beyond the Middle East. 

President Trump says the US military has bombed a small island off the coast of Iran which is home to one of the country’s most important oil terminals. Frank Gardner, the BBC’s security correspondent, explains how both the US and Iran are trying to secure their oil interests in the region. 

Plus Steve Rosenberg joins Laura from Moscow to talk about the US decision to loosen sanctions on Russian oil as the world deals with rising prices. But, what will this mean for Russia’s own war in Ukraine?
